title: A Spider Lives Underwater by Building Its Own Air Bubble
subject: diving bell spider

scenes.text: A spider lives underwater. It brings its own air.
The diving bell spider traps air in a silk web, and the bubble becomes its home.
The bubble works like a physical gill, pulling oxygen out of the surrounding water.
A resting spider in an average bell can stay under for more than a day.
The air doesn't run out of oxygen first. Nitrogen slowly leaks out and the bubble shrinks.
So it swims up, grabs fresh air, and goes back down. A spider with a gill made of silk.

description:
The diving bell spider builds an underwater silk bell filled with air.
The bubble works like a physical gill, and a resting spider can stay under for more than a day.
Would you live in an air bubble underwater?
first_comment: This spider lives in Europe's ponds. What's the strangest home you've seen an animal build?
